items.title: Smart Cut Issues
items.body:
I have noticed what I believe to be a few issues while trying out vidcutter. Mostly they are related to smart cuts. They are as follows:

    1. As of November 5, the ffmpeg call (videoservice.py; line 266) moved the duration arg (-t) to before the input file causing the output clip to be the wrong length for some cases.

    2. If, for example, a clip starts on a key frame causing the 'start' element to be None, the join and the cleanup fail due to an exception trying to use None as a file name. This also causes the overall process to fail silently.

    3. There appears to be a frame gap that occurs between the 'start' and 'middle' elements after a join. This seems to be variable in size, but causes a slight pause when showing the result.

Item 2 had me thinking that smart cut simply did not work, because it also created other discrepancies.

Hope this is of use.

items.title: Add ability to force stream-copy
items.body:
Hi,
sometimes (like in audiovisual archiving institution), one needs a really lossless cut (not reencode), so there should be an option (a button like SmartCut perhaps?) to force stream-copy.

The cutting logic it's trivial (just add condition here):
https://github.com/ozmartian/vidcutter/blob/793127c521b18f0bab19b67bc42e8da16a667afd/vidcutter/libs/videoservice.py#L297

Keep up the good work!

PS: or what about just dropping the reencode and doing -c copy by default? :)

items.title: Vidcutter crashes instantly after opening any videofiles
items.body:
Description: Vidcutter starts up fine, but as soon as I try to open any videofile (doesn't matter if it is MPEG2, MPEG4, avi, whatever) the application crashes/closes itself instantly. The crashes happen with SD- & HD-videos and every videoformat-/container I tested it with. Tried it with smart-cut on/off and Hardware-decoding on/off, but both didn't make a difference. 

Starting Vidcutter via terminal gives no output at all when it crashes, therefore I started Vidcutter with strace. This part at the end seems to be relevant and led to the crashes: 

openat(AT_FDCWD, "/lib64/tls/GL", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/lib64/GL", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/usr/lib64/tls/GL", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
openat(AT_FDCWD, "/usr/lib64/GL", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) = -1 ENOENT (No such file or directory)
munmap(0x7f9c866a8000, 145880)          = 0
--- SIGSEGV {si_signo=SIGSEGV, si_code=SEGV_MAPERR, si_addr=NULL} ---
+++ killed by SIGSEGV (core dumped) +++
Speicherzugriffsfehler (Speicherabzug geschrieben)

Speicherzugriffsfehler = Segmentation fault 

The problem is that vidcutter (or any dependency) try to dlopen the unversioned libGL.so whereas it should use libGL.so.1.
